<h1 align="center">CASTAWAY</h1>

<p align="center">
  <b>A ten-hour lo-fi island video. The right command is always WAIT.</b><br>
  One young woman in cream headphones, one tall palm, one raft. She idles and nods to the beat.
  Every so often, on the bar, something happens. Then she idles again.<br>
  <sub>Working title. In development; no video is published yet. An unofficial remake inspired by the small-island routines and visual comedy of the 1992 screensaver <i>Johnny Castaway</i>.</sub>
</p>

```sh
python tools/serve.py    # then open http://127.0.0.1:8765/
```

**Castaway** is a stationary-frame lo-fi video for YouTube, in the spirit of the ten-hour lofi streams: 16:9, 1080p, 30 fps, sunny, hand-painted and always daytime. Mostly she nods along to her headphones, which is the point. Then, on the next bar of the music, a shark in headphones surfaces and nods along with her. A delivery drone drops off a parcel, and the parcel is another pair of headphones. Once in a very long while she walks out over the water and comes back with an iced coffee. More than 90 activities in [activities.toml](activities.toml), on four timers plus chained follow-ups, decide what happens and when, and every sound is synthesized from code by [tools/make_audio.py](tools/make_audio.py).

The screen above is drawn as a late-80s Japanese computer adventure: a framed, dithered picture, a menu of verbs and a message window that types. It is the right genre for a video in which you mostly wait, because here waiting is a command, and it is the right one.

<details>
<summary><b>見る LOOK</b> &nbsp;the complete walkthrough</summary>
<br>

```text
CASTAWAY : COMPLETE WALKTHROUGH (SPOILERS)
==========================================

  1. LOOK ......... An island. A palm. A raft. Her, nodding.
  2. TALK ......... Greyed out. There is nobody to talk to.
  3. WAIT ......... On the next bar, something happens.
  4. WAIT ......... Something else happens. Or it does not.
  5. LISTEN ....... Kalimba. Electric piano. Crackle. Nodding.
  6. LEAVE ........ She could. She goes for an iced coffee instead.
  7. WAIT ......... Repeat for ten hours.

  You have completed CASTAWAY.
  There was nothing to complete. Well done.
```

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>待つ WAIT</b> &nbsp;four timers, every start on the bar</summary>
<br>

Everything she and her visitors can do lives in [activities.toml](activities.toml): more than 90 activities, each with its step-by-step beats, how long it lasts and how often it comes round. Each tier has its own timer. The typical counts are the median of 200 simulated 10-hour runs, as the file's own header gives them:

```text
TIER          COMES ROUND EVERY          TYPICAL 10-HOUR RUN
------------  -------------------------  -------------------
regular       2 to 5 minutes             ~155
occasional    12 to 25 minutes            ~30
rare          30 to 60 minutes            ~13
super rare    3 to 6 hours, max 3 a run    ~2
chained       set off by another one     follow-ups on top
```

She is busy about a third of the time and idles the rest. Every activity starts on the next bar of the music, every 3 seconds, so the gags land on the beat. Lanes let things overlap, so a ship can sail past while she is busy with a coconut. The default run is `10:00:00` with seed `1992`. `python tools/schedule.py` validates the file and simulates a run.

Around her the scene keeps itself busy: shore waves and drifting cloud shadows are built; distant birds, planes with vapour trails, whale pods, dolphins, sailboats, sandpipers, a gecko and a rain shower are on the way.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>出る LEAVE</b> &nbsp;what might happen while you are not looking</summary>
<br>

- A message in a bottle that washes straight back to her feet. Later, a different bottle brings a reply.
- A delivery drone. The parcel is another pair of headphones.
- A sea turtle comes to visit.
- A grey tabby with a white chest arrives on a crate, climbs the palm and naps. One day it floats away again, and another day it comes back.
- The signal hunt: one bar of signal, at the very top of the palm.
- A shark in headphones, nodding to the same beat.
- A tour boat full of people taking selfies.
- A coconut falls on a hermit crab. Then the coconut walks off, with the crab wearing it.
- She could leave any time: she walks out over the water and comes back with an iced coffee. Super rare, at most once a run, never explained.
- A bro on an electric hydrofoil throws a shaka and carves off.
- Bushcraft: fire by friction, a hammock, a lookout up the palm, spear fishing.
- A kumara, planted, that grows over the course of the video.
- And the regulars: coconut sipping, fishing, jogging laps, waving for rescue, and a sandcastle that stays until the tide takes it.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>聞く LISTEN</b> &nbsp;every sound, from code</summary>
<br>

Every sound is synthesized by [tools/make_audio.py](tools/make_audio.py): more than 150 sound files, and no samples, stock loops or recordings, so no third-party licence applies. The theme is a seamless 60-second loop at 80 BPM in F major (ii, V, I, vi), 20 bars of exactly 3 seconds, with electric piano, a kalimba lead, soft drums and vinyl crackle. The ocean ambience is a seamless 60-second loop too. The mix sits at -14 LUFS with true peak at or below -1 dBTP, and the levels are adjustable for the whole mix and per routine.

Nobody has listened to any of it yet. The numbers are all in order. The numbers would like that noted.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>実行 RUN</b> &nbsp;the tools</summary>
<br>

```sh
python tools/serve.py             # preview and export: http://127.0.0.1:8765/
python tools/schedule.py          # validate the schedule, simulate 10 hours
python tools/render_demo.py --dev # a dev reel of every activity, with a HUD
python tools/make_audio.py        # synthesize every sound again
```

The renderer is [a web page](web/index.html) of plain ES modules: no build step and no npm packages. It previews live and exports frame-exact video in the browser (WebCodecs H.264, 68 to 78 frames a second at 1080p30 in Chrome); the server mixes the sound and joins the two into a YouTube-ready MP4. `tools/render_demo.py` is the older Python reference renderer. Hard cuts and stepped movement are the motion defaults, which is also how this screen moves.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>How this screen is drawn</b></summary>
<br>

It keeps the rules of the machines it imitates. The screen is 640 by 400, exactly the 80 by 25 grid of 8 by 16 character cells: the status line sits on the top row and the prompt on the bottom one. The picture uses exactly 16 colours, each a 12-bit value of the kind a 4096-colour palette allows (`#000 #fff #148 #36b #8cf #199 #6dc #fe9 #c96 #f76 #fca #742 #2a4 #052 #fec #879`), and every other shade is faked with ordered 4 by 4 dither patterns of two of them: the sky, the sea, the clouds, the sand, the title. The title, the palm, the raft, her and every visitor get a hard one-pixel black outline. The menu, the status box and the messages sit on a separate text layer that may only use the eight pure digital colours (the greyed-out TALK and the shadow under the katakana belong to the picture), from an 8 by 16 half-width font and a handful of 16 by 16 kana and kanji, all drawn pixel by pixel in the generator (yes, the zero has a slash).

The menu reads 見る (look), 話す (talk), 待つ (wait), 聞く (listen), 出る (leave) and 実行 (run, as in execute). The question in the LEAVE scene, 島から出ますか？, asks whether you will leave the island; はい is yes and いいえ is no. キャストアウェイ under the title is "castaway" in katakana.

The banner loops every 60 seconds, the length of the theme: 20 bars of 3 seconds at 80 BPM. Every four bars the cursor picks the next command, on the bar, and the window types the answer one character at a time; she nods on every beat, the bar counter counts the 20 bars, and nothing tweens. At the loop point the picture is wiped and redrawn one interlaced line in eight at a time, like a picture being loaded. Under reduced motion the screen holds still on its first frame, with the first message already typed.

</details>
